# Runtime changes in the vendored ScarletNX

ScarletNX is part of this repository (`engine`, from upstream commit 8efbf9c4). The changes below
were patch files before. They are now ordinary commits in the source, and the patch files are deleted. The names
`0001` to `0017` are the old patch numbers. The text says what each change does.

| Change | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| cleanup-issues-100-103-108 | Clean-up of issues #100, #103 and #108. Removed the unused `snx_objects_pack_write`, `gui_games_scan`, the `room_ok` field and `snx_dump_name`, with their tests. The AppImage comment, the build information comment and the data folder of `tools/run_game.py` use the NXAevora name and folder, and the release file names stay as the CI reads them. The GUI strings and the comments of `game_ini.h` name the decrypted game folder, and the translations drop the iOS string and the `src/gui/apple.m` reference. |
| remove-apple-android-frontends | Phase 7.5, unit 1.5 PR B. Removed: the Android, iOS and macOS frontends, their build support and the Mach-O linker, with their docs, scripts, presets and tests. The Windows build and the Linux host build stay (the engine built for Linux, which plays Switch games). |
| remove-guest-drivers | Phase 7.5, unit 1.5 PR A. Removed: the GBA, 3DS, Vita and Linux AArch64 ELF (gnuabi) guest drivers, with their build options (`SNX_BUILD_AGB`, `SNX_BUILD_3DS`, `SNX_BUILD_VITA`, `SNX_BUILD_GNUABI`), tests, tools, scripts, docs, GUI entries and translations, the `swipc --ctr` mode, and the shared code that only they used. The Switch driver stays, and so do the Linux host build (the engine built for Linux, which plays Switch games) and `common/cpu/arm` (the Switch 32-bit module path). Kept GUI and `game_ini`: a folder whose `.ini` says a console other than the Switch (`snx_game_system` returns `SNX_SYSTEM_OTHER`) is refused by `launch`, with a shown message that names the folder and says that ScarletNX plays Switch games only, and the recent games list keeps only `switch` entries (an old line of another word is skipped on load). |
| engine-names | Phase 7.5, PR unit 1b. The program file is `nxaevora-engine` (`nxaevora-engine.exe` on Windows) and the Switch driver name is `nxaevora-engine-switch`. The shown name is `NXAevora Engine` in the window title, the message boxes, the fatal text and the log header. The data folder is `nxaevora` (`.nxaevora` beside a portable copy), and an older `scarletnx` folder is only logged, not migrated: `data: an old .scarletnx folder beside the program is not used (no migration)` or `data: the old user data folder (%APPDATA%\scarletnx) is not used (no migration)`. The icon is `dist/icons/nxaevora-engine.ico` (16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256) and `dist/icons/nxaevora-engine.png` (128x128), made from `assets/nxaevora-engine-icon.png` with Pillow 12.3.0 and Lanczos. The log summary reads the new and the old header. |
| cli-subcommands | Phase 7.5, unit 3 PR 3b. The first argument selects `recompile`, `run` or `settings list`, translated to the old options before the driver reads them (`src/nx/runtime/command.c`, `snx_command_translate`). The old flags stay as aliases. `logs` and `cache` stop with exit 2 until their command exists. The play path checks each recompile-only `--KEY=VALUE` with `ini_check` before the stamp decides that the game is made, so a bad value gives the recompile path's message and exit 2 instead of starting the game. Tests: `runtime_cli_commands`, `driver_workflow`. |
| cli-settings-commands | Phase 7.5, unit 3 PR 3c. `settings schema`, `settings get`, `settings set` and `settings check` (`src/nx/runtime/settings_cli.c`). `schema` prints one JSON document, `{"v":1,"settings":[...]}`, made at run time from the generated tables of `settings.txt`: `key`, `section`, `page`, `type`, `min`, `max`, `default`, `words`, `label`, `help` and `scope` (`startup` or `in-game` from the row's flags, `launcher` for the launcher's table, `recompile` for the recompiler's and LLVM's). The in-game rows are in it. `get` and `set` read and write `<config>/<id>.ini` with `ini_read`, `options.c`'s store and `write_file` (`snx_setting_row`, `snx_settings_load`, `snx_settings_value`, `snx_settings_save`), with no window, no game start and no poll. `check` uses `ini_check` alone. `main.c`'s `name_game` and `game_dirs` are now `snx_game_locate` and `snx_game_folders` (`main.h`), so the commands find the same file. The exit codes are `exit_codes.h`'s: 2 for the usage, 3 for a missing `.ini` or a `--game` that names no game, 7 for a refused value, 1 for a read or write that fails. `--help` comes alone for the five settings words. Tests: `runtime_settings_commands`, `runtime_cli_commands`. |
| cli-progress-stream | Phase 7.5, unit 3 PR 3d. `--progress=jsonl` on `recompile` and `run` (`common/utilities/progress.c`): stdout carries only JSON Lines and the human text goes to stderr (`snx_progress_open` duplicates fd 1 to a private stream, then makes fd 1 a copy of fd 2; on Windows it also sets the standard output handle). The lines are `start`, `progress` with `value` and `total`, `done`, `error` with `message` and `code`, and the exit line `{"v":1,"event":"exit","code":N}`. The stages are `input`, `recompile`, `build`, `prepare`, `start` and `run`; `extract` and `link` are not written. The driver writes `input` and the exit line, and gives `--progress=jsonl-stage` to its child stages, which write no exit line. `snx_error` keeps the last text (`snx_progress_note_error`), `fatal_code` and `process_exit` write the error line of the open stage, with `game_code` for the game's own code, and `snx_report_unit` writes the `recompile` progress line. Tests: `progress_stream`, `runtime_progress_commands`. |
| cli-console-and-progress-fixes | `--skip`, `--settings`, `--migrate` and the host-tools message call `snx_tool_console` before they write, so a Windows console shows them (`entry.c`, `driver/main.c`, `ini_list` in `options.c`). A crash writes its open stage's error line with `snx_progress_crash_error`, a lock-free raw write for the crashed thread (`progress.c`, `fatal_code` in `plat.c`). The parent clears its noted error only when the child ended by itself with a nonzero code; after an interrupt, a signal-ended child or a failed start it keeps the text, and `snx_progress_stage_name` names the child's next stage for that error (`SNX_CHILD_*`, `driver.c`). `run --game=PATH` is refused; the bare `--game=PATH` stays the old form (`USAGE.md`, `engine-ui-plan.md`). The `run_split` test helper runs its child in the given folder on Windows, sets `FD_CLOEXEC` and closes the saved descriptors on failure. Tests: `runtime_cli_commands`, `progress_stream`, `llvm_module`. |
| progress-stream-cleanup | `snx_progress_open_stage` and `snx_progress_is_option` have one copy each in `progress.c`. `run` and `recompile`, also the automatic driver path and `-r`, open the stream after their option checks, so a usage error gives exit 2 and no stream line. On POSIX the private stream descriptor has `FD_CLOEXEC`. `snx_progress_child_redirect` and `snx_progress_child_restore` return the `dup2` error and `driver.c` reports it. The forked child of `snx_run_ticking` checks its `dup2`. The crash writer uses the stored descriptor (`stream_fd`), writes the code without `vsnprintf`, keeps its closing fields after a long message and loops on a short write. `run_split` on Windows opens its files with `_O_NOINHERIT` and clears the inherit flag of the saved handles. Issues #106, #113, #116, #118, part of #114. Tests: `progress_stream`, `runtime_progress_commands`, `os_error`, `platform_log`, `unattended_script`, `llvm_module`. |
| cli-text-and-tests | `dump_exit_code` is now `snx_dump_exit_code` (`driver.h`). The usage names the long forms `--recompile` and `--help`, and `-r, --recompile` once. `--help` with another word is refused with a message that names that word (`snx_command_help`). The usage of `settings get` and `settings set` names exit 1, 2 and 3. No exit code changes. `runtime_cli_commands` compares the whole refusal line and an empty stdout, and runs `run` with `--` and with `--KEY=VALUE`. `runtime_settings_commands` adds an empty `--game=`, a fractional value, the `KEY_MAX` and `VALUE_MAX` limits with a read back of the long value, and the `--help` message. `loader_native` checks that a dump to an output below a regular file is `SNX_DUMP_OUTPUT`. Tests: `runtime_cli_commands`, `runtime_settings_commands`, `loader_native`, `driver_workflow`. |
| decrypted-docs | Phase 7, PR unit 4. Docs and translations only, no runtime change. The ScarletNX docs (`README.md`, `docs/USAGE.md` and the other docs) describe the decrypted game folder that `-r` recompiles, the `romfs=` setting and that `-r` does not play, the text of keys, NSP, XCI, extraction and hactool is removed, and the NXAevora `README.md` lists the feature while the `ROADMAP.md` marks phase 7 as done. The `romfs` help in `src/nx/runtime/settings.txt` no longer names a dump, the comments in `dist/` no longer name dumps and keys, and the 8 stale ids in `po/pt-BR.po` and `po/zh-Hans-CN.po` with the wide glyph U+91CC that only they used are removed. |
| remove-dump-input | Phase 7, PR unit 2. ScarletNX no longer reads encrypted dumps. Removed: hactool (`src/nx/runtime/driver/hactool/`), the container and extraction code (`container.c`, `extract.c`), the keys (`prod.keys`, `title.keys`, the `snx_keys_*` functions, the Keys step of the first-start setup in the terminal and the GUI, the Install Keys menu item), BKTR, the DLC read from a dump, the options `-x`/`--extract`, `--tmpfs`, `--extract-container`, `--keys` and `--title-keys`, the settings `tmpfs` and `extract`, and their tests (`extract`, `hactool_decrypted`, `hactool_layers`). The recompile and the driver refuse an `.nsp`, `.xci`, `.dnsp` or `.dxci` input with a line that names `-r <folder>` (`snx_refuse_encrypted_dump`). `fs_init` stops when the game's data folder has no `exefs/`, because such a folder was made from a dump. It logs the old `source=` first. A program made from an update dump (`<id>_<update id>v<version>`) stops too: `fs_init` checks the update's own data folder for `exefs/` before it lays it over the game's, and the driver refuses such a program for play and for `-r`. The decrypted folder holds the updated game, and the base program made from it replaces the update program. A DLC is read only from an image extracted in its data folder. cJSON moves to `src/nx/runtime/driver/cjson/` (MIT, license installed from its header). The GUI loads only an `.nro` ("Load Switch NRO"). Games no longer asks the driver for a dump's icon (`-x --icon`), and the step list no longer reads the MB rows of an extraction. The `source=` and `--tmpfs` parts of the row romfs-folder are no longer true. Tests: `dump_input`, `filesystem_no_exefs`, `filesystem_update_no_exefs`, `driver_workflow`, `gui_steps`, `runtime_module_abi`, `filesystem_mods_image` (with `tests/romfs_synth.h`). |
| romfs-folder | Phase 7, PR unit 1. `scarletnx -r <folder>` on a decrypted game folder (`ExeFS/`, `RomFS/`, `control.nacp`) no longer copies the RomFS into the data folder. The recompile writes the absolute path of the RomFS folder as `romfs=` in `[Game]` of the game's `.ini` (`snx_record_romfs`), and removes a `romfs/`, `romfs.bin` or `romfs.copying` that an older version left in the data folder. It refuses an input whose ExeFS is inside the data folder (an old data folder as the input) before it removes anything, so the user's only copy is never removed (the loader takes the RomFS beside the ExeFS). At startup `fs_init` grafts the folder as `romfs:/` (`romfs_from_setting` in `fs.c`). A game that reads its dump (`source=`) keeps its dump and logs that `romfs=` is not used. An add-on's RomFS (the update's data folder or a checked DLC) replaces the game's RomFS as before, and the game logs that `romfs=` is not used. A data folder of the game with its own `romfs/` or `romfs.bin` on disk and a `romfs=` setting, or a `romfs=` that is not a folder, stop the game with a log line that names the paths. The recompile option `--tmpfs` is still accepted and does nothing, because the recompile copies no RomFS. Tests: `driver_workflow`, `filesystem_romfs_setting*`, `native_recompiler`. |
| mod-layer | Phase 7, PR unit 3. Test and docs only, no runtime change. The host test `filesystem_mods_setting` lays two mods over a game RomFS that `romfs=` names (outside the data folder): the later mod in name order wins, a mod in `mods_off=` is left out, and the folder of the user is not changed. `docs/USAGE.md` (Mods) tells the byte order of the mod names and that mods lie over the `romfs=` folder too. |
| nvn-folders | Layout only, no code change. The NVN files of `src/nx/gpu` are in `gpu/nvn/` (the native path), `gpu/nvn/diag/` (trace, measure and draw record) and `gpu/nvn/test/` (the in-game selftest and exectest). Their host tests are in `tests/nvn/`, and the helpers of those tests in `tests/nvn/support/`. |
| gui-sdl-step-taken | Test only. The fake driver of `gui_sdl_events` (`wait_taken` in `tests/gui_sdl.c`) takes a `<file>.step` only when its `remove` succeeds. On Windows the remove fails while the test still has the file open, the file stayed, and the next block passed at once, so the percent jumped over the value that `job_step` waited for. A probe that held the file open for 100 ms made the old code fail each time and the new code pass. |
| nvn-compute-qmd-size-limits | The native compute QMD builder refuses a constant buffer size that would lose bits when packed into the 17-bit size field. Uniform slots 0 to 4 are checked after 256-byte rounding, and program constant buffer 1 is checked after its existing padding. Driver-only uniform slots keep their 32-bit size limit. A refusal leaves the output untouched and identifies the uniform slot. Test `nvn_params` checks the boundaries, wraparound sizes and driver-only descriptors without game files. Update 1.1.1 recompiles and runs. The established path renders the opening dialogue. Native-path captures are black with both the original and patched builder, and a 120 s patched run reaches no compute dispatch. The compute gameplay effect is not verified. |
| 0001-native-mouse-input | Native mouse input. The mouse is captured and drives the right stick. The left button is ZR and the right button is ZL. A controller input makes the controller the active input. Hold Alt to free the cursor. New settings `mouse_*` (look, sensitivity, vertical sensitivity, invert Y, dead zone offset, curve, overdrive). See `docs/records/input/input-analysis.md` and `docs/records/input/camera-analysis.md`. |
| 0002-global-red-add-u64 | Shader translation of `RED.E.ADD.64` (a 64-bit add into global memory, size 2 of `RED`). The translator refused it, so one draw in each frame was skipped. The module declares `Int64Atomics`, each global buffer gets a 64-bit view on the same binding (decoration `Aliased`), and the device enables `shaderBufferInt64Atomics`. A device without the feature refuses the program as before. A regression test with a `spirv-val` check is in `tests/shader_direct_regressions.c`. See `docs/records/graphics/shader-analysis.md`. |
| 0009-keyboard-remap | The keyboard map as a setting. The new setting `keyboard_map` (section Keyboard) lists `Button:Key` words, for example `ZL:Q A:F LStickUp:Up`. A button that the text names loses its default keys. A key that the text names belongs only to the buttons named with it. `None` frees a button. A key name is the SDL name, with `_` for a space. Escape, F1 to F12, Pause and Alt are reserved. A word that cannot be read is logged and the map stays. See `docs/records/input/input-analysis.md`. |
| 0010-ini-store-256 | The store of the game's `.ini` held 128 keys, and the file already had 129 (the log said `more than 128 keys, renderdoc_frames and those after it are left out`). A key after the 128th was dropped at the read and so erased at the next write of the file. A key that the user added, such as `keyboard_map`, went this way. The limit is now 256. A write puts at most 256 key rows in the file: when the store's keys and the rows with a default do not fit, `write_file` writes only the store's keys and says so with one `WARN` that names the two counts and the limit, so the next start reads the file whole. |
| 0012-native-mouse-guest-words | The runtime side of the native mouse look. The setting `mouse_native_address` (0 = off) is the guest address of a 64 bit word (two floats: yaw in radians, pitch in units of the camera arc). The mouse motion is added to it as it arrives, in place of the stick, and the game's code patch `native-mouse-look.pchtxt` takes it. Settings `mouse_native_yaw` (1400) and `mouse_native_pitch` (1000, 500 from `0016`), in millionths for each mouse count, and `mouse_invert_x` and `mouse_invert_y` turn the directions. At most 0.5 of each waits for the game. See `docs/records/input/camera-analysis.md`. |
| 0013-imgui-windows | The in-game Dear ImGui windows (plan: `docs/records/ui/imgui-plan.md`, review: `docs/records/archive/imgui-review.md`). It is one patch of ten steps that were once separate patches. Dear ImGui 1.93.0 (MIT) is a pinned CPM package (`cmake/dependencies.cmake`, SHA-256 of the release archive). The core and the Vulkan backend (loaded through volk) are built into the renderer and draw a frame over the presented image (`gpu/vk/imgui.c`, `imgui_glue.cpp`). The fonts are read from `fonts/` in the game's data folder (`Roboto-Variable.ttf`, `NotoSansJP-Regular.otf`, from `assets/fonts`), and the built-in font is the fallback. The theme is ImGui's dark theme with the accent `#46478B` and an alpha of 0.94 on the whole window (`imgui_style.cpp`). The window's events go to a queue (`imgui_input.c`, `backend/imgui_sdl.c`) that merges motion and never drops a key, button or focus change, and the frame publishes what the windows want (mouse, keyboard, text, release of the cursor, the input method's place). A menu bar (About, Settings, Mods, Cheats, Debug) shows when the cursor is at the top of the picture, and Alt frees the cursor from the mouse look. The Debug window shows the GPU (NVML, picked by the Vulkan device's UUID), the processor and memory, the frame times, the cost of a frame and the display. The game's software keyboard (the player's name) is a window too: `overlay.c` keeps the state and the ticket protocol, and the old box returns when the windows do not run or the Vulkan backend reports an error. The windows replace the game's old menu (F2, Back, Home, the on-screen menu button), and `legacy_menu` brings it back. New settings `imgui` (default 1), `imgui_test` and `legacy_menu` (default 0), section Debug. While the game presents nothing for a quarter second (a loading interval), the renderer's refresh also runs when the windows have something drawn or an input event waits, so the windows keep updating and the menu bar still opens. |
| 0014-gui-group-icons | The launcher test `gui_sdl_events` wants an icon for the group of each section of `settings.txt`. The sections Mouse (`0001`) and Keyboard (`0009`) had none, so the test failed. Mouse gets the pointer icon and Keyboard the key icon. |
| 0015-imgui-input-test | The host test `imgui_input` for the event queue of the ImGui windows: positions and wheel steps merge, the order of events holds, a full queue removes motion and keeps a key, a button or a focus change. |
| 0016-settings-controller-keyboard | The window "Controller&Keyboard" of the ImGui windows (menu Settings, same name for the entry). It is one patch of five steps that were once separate patches. The pages are the sections Mouse and Keyboard of `settings.txt` (the list `PAGES` in `imgui_settings.c`), and a row is made from the setting's table row, so the window and the `.ini` cannot differ. An int with words is a choice, an int is a slider (a field when its range is wider than 100000), a float is a slider, and the help of the setting is the tooltip. A startup setting says that it applies at the next start, and a setting that the command line holds is disabled. A change waits in a small queue (`backend_setting_request`) and the main thread applies it in `video_poll` through the new `options_change` (`options.c`): `ini_check`, the same apply as a reload, then `ini_set`. The row `mouse_native_address` is not shown (a guest address that the launcher sets). While the pointer is over a slider or a choice, Left and Right move it by the setting's step (Shift: ten steps, Ctrl: one unit), and the window asks for the keyboard, so the game gets no arrow key. The Keyboard page has the key bindings: the 24 buttons with the keys that send them (a default key is dimmed), Bind (the next key press, taken in `video_poll` by scancode before the windows and the game see it, Esc cancels, F1 to F12, Pause and Alt are not taken), None, Default and Reset all. The window leaves the new text of `keyboard_map` for the main thread, which applies it with `options_change` (`g_keybind` belongs to that thread). A capture ends on Esc, on a loss of the focus and on a key that has no name that gives the same key back, and the bindings follow a `--keyboard_map` on the command line. Each key's release clears the buttons that its own press set. `keyboard_map_set` is split in `keybind_compile`, which the view uses too. The patch also sets the defaults: the keys A: F, B: Left Shift, X: R, Y: Space, L3: Left Ctrl, L: Q, R: E, Plus: G, Minus: M, the arrow keys for the D-pad and W, A, S, D for the left stick (ZL, ZR, R3 and the right stick have no key), the F1 help text, and `mouse_native_pitch` 500 (was 1000). The menu bar no longer comes up for a popup of another window (a combo closed at once because the bar took the focus), and it stays hidden when the program starts with the cursor outside the window (`imgui_sdl.c` gives the windows a position only when the window has the mouse focus, and no position when the cursor leaves it). The Controllers page (the section Controllers) shows the rows that every player shares (swap A/B, stick dead zone, vibration, background input, Joy-Con pairing) and the button map: for each of the 16 controls of a gamepad, a choice of the console button that it sends (None, A to Down). A button that another control sends goes to the old control of this one, so no button is lost. The map is `gamepad_map` (A and B swapped as `gamepad_swap_ab` says), "Reset to the console's layout" clears it, and the main thread saves it with `options_change` (`backend_padmap_request`). The rows of each player (`gamepad_pN_*`) are not shown, and a player's own `gamepad_pN_map` is not edited. |
| 0017-display-window | The window "Display" (menu Settings), with the tabs Display, Graphics and Performance (sections of `settings.txt`). The pages carry the window that shows them (`imgui_settings.c`), and one function draws both windows. A setting that is chosen from a short list is a combo box: the resolution scale (0.5x to 4x, with the size at 1920 x 1080 for 1x) and the anisotropic filtering (the game's, 2x to 16x); a value that is not in the list shows as custom. A startup setting that the window changed shows the saved value and "Saved. Start the game again to apply it." (`options_restart_value`, kept by `options_change`). `vsync` has three values: 0 off (immediate, else mailbox, else FIFO), 1 on (FIFO, the default), 2 on (mailbox, else FIFO). The Debug window shows the size the game renders at (scaled) and the V-sync mode. The picture's alpha is made 1 before it is presented, with a pipeline that writes only alpha (`ui.c`): the game's alpha channel made the HUD leave ghosts over the picture with mailbox and immediate (`docs/records/graphics/present-alpha.md`). The Display and Performance tabs moved to the engine menu (row `engine-menu-display-pages`), the Graphics tab moved too (row `engine-menu-graphics-page`), and the window is deleted. |
| 0018-fxaa | The setting `anti_aliasing` (section Graphics, 0 off, 1 FXAA, default 0) and the pass `postfx.c`. The frame that the game presents goes through one fragment pass into an image of its own (same format and size as the render target), and the present blits from that image. The on-screen controls and the windows are drawn after the pass. The render targets and the guest memory stay as the game drew them. The shader `fxaa.frag` is a new implementation of the edge-directed blur of the FXAA whitepaper (Timothy Lottes, NVIDIA, 2009). The Graphics page of the engine menu shows the mode in the row Anti-aliasing. |
| 0019-scaling-filter | The setting `scaling_filter` (section Graphics, 0 bilinear, 1 bicubic, default 0). Bilinear is the blit of before. Bicubic draws the frame (or the anti-aliasing image) into the window image over the letterboxed rectangle with a Catmull-Rom filter over 4 x 4 texels (`shaders/bicubic.frag`, `postfx.c`). It filters in gamma space, so an sRGB frame does not ring. The Graphics page of the engine menu shows the filter in the row Scaling. FSR1 and its sharpness are next. |
| 0020-smaa | The value 2 (SMAA) of the setting `anti_aliasing`. `shaders/smaa.frag` is a port to GLSL of SMAA 1x from SMAA.hlsl (Jimenez, Echevarria, Masia, Navarro, Gutierrez, MIT, the license is in `dist/smaa/LICENSE.txt`), preset HIGH, luma edges, no predication or temporal parts. It builds three passes with macros: the edges (RG8 image, cleared to zero, luma taken in gamma space for an sRGB frame), the blending weights (RGBA8 image, with the area and search tables) and the blending into the anti-aliasing image of `postfx.c`. The two tables are the DX9 area texture and the search texture of the SMAA repository, embedded by `cmake/smaa_tables.cmake` from `dist/smaa/`, where the test `tracked_material` allows binary files. `postfx.c` now keeps its images as `Target` and draws every pass with `fullscreen_pass`. |
| 0021-nvn-submit-trace | With `nvn_trace=1`, the first 40 GPFIFO submissions are logged (`gpu-submit:` lines): the channel, the number of entries, the syncpoint increments, the fence, the first entries and the last entry with its first 24 words. It shows what a queue call adds to the command buffers of the game (phase 6, `docs/records/graphics/nvn-survey.md`). Nothing changes when the setting is 0. |
| 0022-nvn-diagnostic-3a | With `nvn_trace=1`, the first 3 GPFIFO submissions list every entry and show all words of the entries of 64 words or fewer (the entries that the NVN library adds). The first 40 calls of `nvnTextureBuilderGetStorageSize` and `GetStorageAlignment` log the result and 128 bytes of the builder (`nvn-size:` lines). It is the diagnostic of step 3a (`docs/records/graphics/nvn-design.md`, 2-6). Nothing changes when the setting is 0. |
| 0023-nvn-native-base | The setting `nvn_native` (startup, 0 or 1, default 0) and `gpu/nvn/nvn_native.c`. With 1 the host hooks `nvnBootstrapLoader` and `nvnDeviceGetProcAddress` below the trace hooks, and puts a host handler in the dispatch slot of each resolved function. No host handler exists yet, so every function gets the missing-function handler: the first call is logged (`nvn-native: not implemented: <name>`) and it returns 0, and the exit report lists the calls. `gpu/nvn/nvn_objtab.c` is the table of the host's records of NVN objects, keyed by guest address (test `nvn_objtab`). With 0 nothing changes. With 1 the game does not draw. Later the change `nvn-legacy-setting` replaced this setting with `nvn_legacy` (default 0 = native path). |

They are the answers that the host handlers must give (phase 6, step 3b). |

Without this step the caller ran its last block again, so `nvnDeviceBuilderSetDefaults` was called more than 10^9 times. |

Both descriptor types share CPU destination lookup. Invalid inputs give one log line and no write. | 0032-nvn-native-windows | With `nvn_native=1`, host records handle window builders, window initialization, interval and crop settings, and sync initialization. `WindowInitialize` reads the texture pointer array at call time, accepts 1 to 4 known texture records, and leaves the window record unchanged on failure. | 0034-nvn-selftest-harness | New setting `nvn_selftest` (needs `nvn_trace=1` and `nvn_native=0`). At the first `nvnQueueInitialize` the selftest calls the library function and the host handler with the same arguments on the calling guest thread, restores the CPU context after each call, and compares the results. Its objects are in a 64 KiB block from `kmem_alloc`, not in the game heap. The comparer (`nvn_selftest_cmp.c`), the arena (`nvn_selftest_mem.c`) and the recording `Renderer` (`nvn_selftest_rec.c`) are pure parts with host tests. The first cases are `nvnDeviceGetInteger` (the word written, kind M) and the texture builder storage size, alignment, width and height (kind R). `nvn_trace.c` gives the library entry by name, and `nvn_native.c` gives the host handler by name. | 0035-nvn-review-p1 | Two fixes from the review of 3b. With `nvn_native=1` and `nvn_trace=1` together, each resolver hook (`nvnDeviceGetProcAddress`) is now installed once. | 0036-nvn-review-p2 | Fixes from the review of 3b. A failed `MemoryPoolInitialize` or `TextureInitialize` removes its record, so later calls cannot use it. `TextureInitialize` fails with a log line when the layout does not fit in the memory pool. Texture and buffer sizes use 64-bit math. The target names are corrected to the library's numbers (5 multisample, 6 multisample array, 7 rectangle), with no change of behavior. A sampler wrap above 7 and a texture swizzle above 5 fail at registration with a log line, and are no longer mapped to a default. `nvnDeviceGetInteger` answers 0 only for a `what` above 0x62 (the library's switch default), and writes nothing for an unknown `what` below it. `WindowAcquireTexture` checks write permission of the index pointer. `SyncWait` on a sync that is not signaled logs the sync, its state and the timeout. The selftest recorder keeps the compute launch description, and the selftest checks guard bytes around the `DeviceGetInteger` output word. The selftest also logs the device bytes at +0x1b18 and +0x1b1c, because the source of the compression switch is not known. | 0039-nvn-native-command-buffers | With `nvn_native=1`, host handlers for sixteen CommandBuffer functions: Initialize, Finalize, SetMemoryCallback, SetMemoryCallbackData, AddCommandMemory, AddControlMemory, BeginRecording, EndRecording, CallCommands, SetTexturePool, SetSamplerPool, SetRenderTargets, SetViewports, SetScissors, ClearColor and Barrier. Now `frame_run` replays the lists through `frame_replay_lists`. |

| 0044-arceus-clock | `runtime/arceus_clock.c`, called from `snx_main` after the NVN trace (`arceus_clock_init`) and after the JIT starts (`arceus_clock_post_jit`). For Pokémon Legends: Arceus 1.1.1 only. It is on by default on that build, and `SNX_ARCEUS_TIMING_FIXES=0` turns it off. With `SNX_ARCEUS_TARGET_FPS` unset it installs nothing while the runtime's frame limit is game pace or 30 FPS and below, unless the legacy `SNX_ARCEUS_FPS60=1` is set, which targets 60 FPS and writes it as the frame limit. A set `SNX_ARCEUS_TARGET_FPS` takes precedence over `SNX_ARCEUS_FPS60`. It moves the game's fixed 1/30 second clocks to the elapsed time of the frame at a target of 60 or 120 FPS, unlocked, or the runtime's own pace (`game`), with separate fixes for the water, effects, event camera, blinks, menu repeat and camera stick. It also turns off the automatic 3D resolution governor by default (`SNX_ARCEUS_FIXED_RESOLUTION`, on unless set to a value other than `1`) and has read-only traces. Each change checks the build id and the instruction words first. See `docs/records/game/arceus-timing.md`. Test `arceus_timing` checks the shared step and the camera stick update. |
| 0045-arceus-physics-step | With `SNX_ARCEUS_PHYSICS_TIMESTEP_FIX=1` and a target rate, the main rigid-body world steps the smaller of 1/30 second and the elapsed time instead of a fixed 1/30 second (`main+2AF25B4`). The cave light increment (`main+1E1A25C`) is scaled for each call. The census skips the owners that a fix wraps and logs the day clock. See `docs/records/game/arceus-timing.md`. |
| 0048-arceus-gravity-probe | With the cadence census on, `SNX_ARCEUS_GRAVITY_PROBE=1` logs `arceus-gravity` lines from the shared acceleration (`main+198D7E4`). | 0049-arceus-capture | With `SNX_ARCEUS_CAPTURE_FIX=1` and a target rate, the waiting stages of the capture director (`main+180C338`) count down 30 times per second of elapsed time instead of once per call. | 0050-arceus-battle-sequence | On by default with a target rate (`SNX_ARCEUS_BATTLE_SEQUENCE_FIX=0` turns it off), a wrapper on the battle effect sequence update (`main+9DBEAC`) passes speed times 30 times the elapsed time for the call and restores the authored speed after it. The step is cut at the next whole frame, so every whole frame is the frame one call ends on and the next is entered on, and the commands' end checks and exact-frame actions run. A call makes one update for a speed up to 1, and the budget keeps at most one game step, so a stall is not caught up. The default (unset or `2`) is the even landing: a step that would end just before a whole frame goes onto it and the difference is carried, so at a 60 FPS limit the frame and the battle camera move evenly. `1` is the plain cut. | nvn-selftest-d1-state | The command buffer selftest compares every 3D register that either side changed from the base state, not a fixed list (`nvn_selftest_regdiff.c`). 29 cases cover the state setters and the state object binds. Each case gets the control memory again, because each `EndRecording` uses it and the library aborts when it runs out (sdk d8243b8). Eight host handlers are logged no-ops by design. Their rows count as expected no-op, and such a row fails when it shows no difference, so that it is checked again. The Blend, ChannelMask and Polygon binds use a draw as the work call, because the host sends them only at a draw. The draw that the front end holds for merging is flushed after each side. Test `nvn_selftest_regdiff`. |
| nvn-selftest-d2-binds | The plural binds (`BindTextures`, `BindImages`, `BindStorageBuffers`) go to the replay in the library packet form, with the high handle word and the fourth zero word of each entry. `SetTexturePool` also writes the texture pool base to the driver constants, as the library interpreter does. The word stream decoder accepts the mode 3 (non-increasing) header. The recording decoder reads the pool records 0x13 and 0x14, and the selftest expands them into the words that the library writes at submission (d84c120, d84c3b0). The vertex attrib and stream state scripts build each element with the setters of their side. 15 selftest cases cover the binds and the resources. The pool and render target address registers differ per side by design and are left out of the diff for those cases only. Tests `nvn_params`, `nvn_replay`, `nvn_cmdlist` and `nvn_selftest_dec`. |
| nvn-selftest-d3-copies | 30 selftest cases cover the draws, clears, copies, downsamples and the uniform upload. The register diff also compares the 2D, DMA and compute engines, with an ignore list per engine for the per-side addresses. A case fails when an engine has more changed registers than a record holds. The host replay sends the 2D open and close words of subchannel 0 to the puller, and the pool binds also write the compute engine. A DMA copy writes the pitch only for the pitch side and the surface words only for the block linear side, with the 8-row GOB height (0x1000) in the block size word (sdk d82b0f0). The 2D route of `CopyBufferToTexture` uses the corner origin and starts the source half a texel in. `Downsample` uses the center origin with the bilinear filter. A new optional `Renderer` hook `engine_write` takes the constant buffer and inline to memory uploads. The selftest recorder sets it, so a selftest job writes no guest memory. The recorder records adjacent writes as one run, with the texture pool address relative to the pool of its side. The Vulkan renderer leaves the hook unset. Tests `nvn_replay`, `nvn_rt`, `nvn_selftest_regdiff` and `nvn_selftest_rec`. |
| nvn-selftest-d4-cpu-side | 27 selftest cases cover the command buffer functions of the CPU side. A new file `nvn_selftest_cbstate.c` makes a new command buffer on each side for each case and compares return values: the getters after Initialize and after each setter, IsRecording around BeginRecording and EndRecording, the checkpoints and SetDebugLabel. The five memory getters that the host refuses are expected refusals. A new S table compares CallCommands, the debug markers and groups, and the two ZCull functions (expected no-op) at a clear. No host handler changed. |
| nvn-queue-fences-exectest | With `nvn_native=1`, NVN syncs are fenced on the syncpoint of the queue: a post promises one increment, the job end increments it after the releases, and `SyncWait` and `QueueFinish` wait on it. `QueueFlush`, `QueueFinish`, and a queue or command buffer fence with `FLUSH_FOR_CPU` post the pending frame as a job without a window. A new `QueueInitialize` fails the syncs of the frame that it drops. `QueueWaitSync` on a pending fence of another queue returns 0 with a log line. The setting `nvn_exectest` (`gpu/nvn/test/nvn_exectest.c`) runs eight cases of real work through the host handlers once after the first `nvnQueueInitialize` and checks the results in memory. Design: `docs/records/graphics/nvn-design.md`, "Queue fences and flush jobs (4-u3-4)". |
| nvn-u4-host-lookup | With `nvn_native=1` the host answers `nvnBootstrapLoader` and `nvnDeviceGetProcAddress` from the name and address tables of the NVN library in the `sdk` module of update 1.1.1 (build ID checked, tables read and checked at the first lookup). The library lookup, which set itself up with the device on each call, no longer runs. The new setting `nvn_native_missing` (default 1) stops the game with the function name when the host has no handler for a called function or the library has no function of a looked-up name. 0 logs it and returns 0 as before. Test `nvn_params`. |
| nvn-u3-5-pure-checks | The checks of six NVN handlers move into pure functions of `nvn_params.c` with host tests: the texture slot of `WindowBuilderGetTexture`, the refusal reasons and the image take of the window acquire, the refusal reasons of `QueuePresentTexture`, the bounds of `SetSampleLocations`, the words that `BindProgram` keeps, and the count, entry and stage checks of `ProgramSetShaders` and `SetShadersExt`. The results, the log lines and the locks of the handlers do not change. |
| ui-fixed-tv-mode | The runtime is always in TV mode. The setting `docked` and the handheld paths are gone: am and apm report the Console operation mode and Boost, am and vi report the TV display mode of 1920 x 1080, and hid has no handheld Npad source. `docked` and `modo_tv` are listed as deprecated keys. | ui-render-resolution | The float scale `resolution` (0.25 to 16) is replaced by the choice `render_resolution`: 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 2160p of the game's 1920 x 1080, as the scales 2/3, 1, 4/3 and 2 (`vk_render_scale` in `scale.h`). The log names the choice at start. The ImGui window shows the 4 choices, each with the GPU memory note when it does not fit. Test `imgui_settings` checks the scales, the 1280 x 720 and 3840 x 2160 sizes and the notes. |
| gfx-scaled-texel-fetch | At a render resolution other than 1080p, a fragment shader that reads a scaled target with TLD at a texel made from FragCoord read only the guest grid (FragCoord times 1/scale, truncated, then times the scale again), so the 3D image looked like a 1080p image upscaled with nearest. Now a slot whose texture has the bound target's aspect ratio takes floor(texel * scale + mod(FragCoord, scale)), the fragment form of Ryujinx's `Helper_TexelFetchScale` (MIT), which gives back the fragment's own pixel. Other scaled slots keep floor((texel + 0.5) * scale). The aspect mask is in push constant words 10 and 11 (`render.c`). Tests: `shader_direct_regressions` (`scaled_texel_fetch`), `imgui_settings` (`vk_scale_same_aspect`). |
| gfx-scaled-layers | A 2D array texture whose layers are separate scaled single-layer render targets (the shadow maps of 1024 x 1024, R8_UINT and D32_SFLOAT) is now read as one group image. The members draw into its layers at the scaled size, so the texture no longer takes a nearest blit down to the guest size. `Surf` has a base layer, and barriers cover only the layers of a member (`vk_barrier_layers`). `vk_rt_group_make` makes the group and moves the members into it, and the last member that leaves frees it. `tex_from_tic` asks `vk_rt_group_for` for header type 5 with one level. A missing, unfit (unscaled, another format or size) or stale member keeps the old path with a log line, and a draw that samples a group that it renders to binds nothing with a log line. The shader needs no change: TLD, TLDS and TXQ of a 2D array already take the scale. Tests: `rt_group`, `shader_direct_regressions` (`scaled_texel_fetch`, the 2D array case). |

| nvn-s4-draw-record | New setting `nvn_drawrec` for the stage 4 compare of `nvn_native=0` and `=1` (`docs/records/graphics/nvn-design.md`, "Stage 4 compare: the draw record"). At start the runtime wraps `g_renderer` and records each draw, clear, dispatch, 2D blit, DMA copy, memory blit, draw texture and present before it forwards the call unchanged. Each call gets a 64-bit signature made only of values that do not depend on the path: counts, topology, formats, sizes and the hash of each shader program (`shader_hash` of the code read with `gmem_read_code`). No GPU address goes into it. The cached hash of a program is checked once for each present with the backend's write tracking and is dropped on a shader instruction invalidate or a renderer reset, because the game writes other programs at the same addresses. Each present appends one line with the call counts and two frame hashes to `<game>.drawrec<N>.frames.txt`, and a table of the signatures with their counts and the text of the first call goes to `<game>.drawrec<N>.sigs.txt` every 600 presents and at a clean exit (`N` is `nvn_native`). An error of a file turns the record off with a log line. Without the setting nothing changes. The pure part is `gpu/nvn/diag/draw_record_sig.c`, test `draw_record`. |
| nvn-s5-measure | New setting `nvn_measure` (startup, 0 or 1, default 0) for the stage 5 CPU measure (`docs/records/graphics/nvn-design.md`, "Stage 5 measure plan", decisions 1 to 4). New module `gpu/nvn/diag/nvn_measure.c` and pure part `gpu/nvn/diag/nvn_measure_calc.c`. With 1, four atomic counters take the monotonic clock around the old path's `gpu_submit` and `run_job` and the native path's `native_call` and `frame_run`; the present is left out of both GPU scopes so they match. The time a handler waits for the GPU (window acquire, sync wait, queue finish) or for the present pace (`present_pace` in the window acquire) is left out of `native_call`, because on the old path these waits run in the game's library or in `vi.c` and not in `gpu_submit`. Each 600 presents the renderer writes one `nvn-measure:` line with the path, the mean guest and GPU milliseconds per frame, the frame time median, 99th percentile and maximum of the window, and the draws and skipped draws. The counters of the other path are also read and reset, and a non-zero value adds `other_ns=` to the line. 0 costs no clock read. With 1 it also times each host handler. A blocked `objs_lock` take adds its wait to a lock counter that the handler's guest time leaves out, and the `nvn-measure:` line gains `lock_ms=`. At a clean exit it writes the 25 handlers with the largest wall time, with their calls, wall time, mean per call, lock wait and other wait, then one totals line. The pure part gets `nvn_measure_top`, which the test `nvn_measure` covers. |
| nvn-lock-holder | With `nvn_measure=1` each take of `objs_lock` writes a holder code (the handler slot, the GPU thread or another thread), and a blocked take reads it before it waits. At a clean exit the report adds one `nvn-measure: lock waiter=` line for the game threads and one for the GPU thread, with the wait split by holder class, a `lock threads=` line with the count of threads that ran a handler, and the 10 handlers that made other threads wait longest. The code is not cleared at unlock, so a waiter can see the previous holder when the lock changes hands in between. `gpu.c` gets `gpu_on_gpu_thread`. The pure codes are in `nvn_measure_calc.c` and the test `nvn_measure` covers them. With 0 nothing changes. |
| nvn-rw-shared-mode | `common/filesystem/host.h` gets `pm_lock_shared`, `pm_unlock_shared` and `pm_trylock_shared` for a `PMutex`: the `SRWLOCK` shared calls on Windows, a normal take on POSIX until the Linux work. A blocked shared take notes its wait for the hang report. The shared calls do not report to the profiler, because the Tracy C API has only an exclusive lockable context. Nothing uses them yet (step 1 of the `objs_lock` split, `docs/records/graphics/nvn-design.md`). Test `host_shared_lock`. |
| nvn-rw-shared-handlers | The command buffer handlers (all except `Initialize` and `Finalize`), `nvnBufferMap`, `nvnBufferGetAddress` and `nvnBufferGetSize` take `objs_lock` in the shared mode (step 3 of the `objs_lock` split, `docs/records/graphics/nvn-design.md`). A command buffer record gets an owner thread id: a shared handler claims it with one compare-and-swap and clears it at the end. When another thread owns it, the handler logs the conflict (the first 8), counts it, and runs under the exclusive mode. A bind of a state object or a vertex state that has no record reads the defaults into a local array and makes no record. The depth range handlers read the device record without making it. The log counters of the command buffers and the lost buffers are atomic. With `nvn_measure=1` the lock lines are split by mode (`mode=exclusive|shared`, `takes=`) and one line gives `command_conflicts=`. Test `nvn_cmdlist` covers the owner claim. `nvnMemoryPoolInitialize` and `nvnMemoryPoolFinalize` do the GPU address allocation, the range maps and unmaps with no `objs_lock`, and take it only to copy the builder and to add or remove the record. |
| nvn-legacy-setting | The native NVN path is the default. The setting `nvn_native` is removed and a debug setting `nvn_legacy` (startup, 0 or 1, default 0) takes its place: 1 runs the game's own NVN library (the old path) as a comparison target. A `.ini` that still has `nvn_native` keeps it under `[Deprecated]` (`ini.c`, `docs/DEPRECATIONS.md`). The draw record file number stays 1 for the native path and 0 for the old path. | blit2d-source-format | A 2D engine blit reads its source in the 2D format, not in the format of the render target at that address. `vk_blit2d` (`surface.c`) took the target's image, and `vkCmdBlitImage` converted from its format: the battle start cross-fade copies the A8B8G8R8 sRGB frame (0xD6) as UNORM (0xD5) into the texture it blends over the next frame, so each frame got an sRGB decode and the picture went to black (issue #44, both NVN paths). The Strong Style and Agile Style cut-ins went black too and are correct with this change. When the image format differs from the 2D source format, the copy is unscaled, the two 2D formats are equal and the texel sizes match, the blit is now a `vkCmdCopyImage` of the bytes, as on the hardware. Other mismatches keep the blit and log one line. Test `check_blit2d_srgb_as_unorm` in `tests/vulkan_headless.c` (built with `SNX_TEST_VULKAN=ON`). |

| cli-exit-codes | Phase 7.5, unit 3 PR 3a. One exit-code table in `src/common/utilities/exit_codes.h` (`SNX_EXIT_*`: 0 success, 1 internal, 2 usage, 3 game files, 4 recompile, 5 start before the window, 6 crash, 7 refused setting, 8 nonzero game code, 130 interrupt) replaces the literal values of the CLI and the runtime start. The recompile's bad option or `--KEY=VALUE` is 2, its missing input or `exefs/main` is 3, and a compile, link, staging or build failure is 4. A GDB stub start failure is 5. `process_exit` ends 0 or 8. `fatal` (`plat.c`) writes to stderr and to the early error file `<state>/scarletnx-error.log` and shows no dialog before the renderer runs, where it exits 5; after it the renderer keeps the box and exits 6, and a crash report always exits 6, before or after the renderer. A missing or unreadable game program ends with 3 through `fatal_game_files`, a small `fatal` variant for that code. A missing or unreadable `_data` folder or `exefs/main` (`fs.c`, `runtime/loader.c`), a `romfs=` that is not a folder or has two sources, a failed graft and an unreadable RomFS image (`fs.c`), and a module of another ABI or variant version (`main.c`) also end with 3 through it. A host memory commit failure while loading the game's executables stays a start failure (5), while a missing or invalid executable stays 3 (`runtime/loader.c`). The dispatch table uses `snx_alloc`, so its allocation failure ends with 1. An existing settings file that cannot be read ends with 5 (`options.c`). The window backend sets the renderer-ready flag after the renderer starts, in a window or headless (`backend/sdl3.c`, `video_init`), and a fatal left for `video_poll` exits 6. A fatal writes the early error file once through `win_fatal_log`, before and after the renderer and in a crash; a log line that is not a fatal does not write it. With no game folder and no state folder, the early file goes to the user's state folder. Tests: `exit_codes`, `runtime_unknown_option` (exact codes), `runtime_recompile_settings` (exact codes), `driver_workflow` (the changed codes). `engine/docs/USAGE.md` has the table. |

A failure to index the game's files exits 1 for `FS_TREE_NOMEM` and 3 for every other status (`fs.c`, through the new `fatal_internal` in `plat.c`). A settings file that is missing gives the defaults, and a read that fails for another reason stops the run (`snx_path_missing` in `common.c`, `options.c`, `game_ini.c`). `--dump-modules` exits 3 when the program cannot be loaded and 1 when the dump cannot be written, from `SnxDumpResult` (`loader.h`). With the text tick on, the "next" prompt at the bottom right of a text box shows for a short time and then goes away, and it is not fixed. See `docs/dev/engine/arceus-timing.md`. |
| ini-partial-no-write | The runtime does not write the settings `.ini` back when the last parse of it was incomplete: more than 256 keys, a key of 64 bytes or more, or a value of 2048 bytes or more. `write_file` reads a static state before it makes the `.tmp` file and returns 1, so `ini_open` and `ini_poll` write nothing in that run. The game's changes stay in the store as dirty entries (row `ini-store-dirty`) and are written when a reload finds the file complete. They are lost at exit only when no such reload comes. Writes start again in the run when a reload finds the file complete, for example after the user removes keys, and at a later start only if the file is complete then. One `WARN` names the file when the state is set, and one `LOG` says when the blocked state ends. `snx_settings_save` (CLI) and the GUI and driver writers are unchanged. |
| arceus-nvn-blend-targets | On by default on native NVN (`SNX_ARCEUS_NVN_BLEND_TARGETS=0` turns it off), the replay keeps one blend state bind for each colour target (bits 0 to 2 of the object's first word, `gpu/nvn/nvn_blend_slots.h`), and the next draw sends every target bound since the last draw in bind order. With one slot only the last bind was sent, so the other targets kept the factors of an earlier draw and the opening cutscene was over-bright. |
| ini-store-dirty | The settings store keeps an in-game change in its entry with a `dirty` flag, in place of the queue of up to 64 changes. `ini_set` marks the entry and no longer drops a change when 64 keys are reached. `write_file` writes a snapshot and clears the flags of the values that it wrote, and a reload copies the dirty entries over the file's values, so a complete reload writes the changes of a blocked run. A change of a new key in a full store is not saved, with one `WARN` (memory keeps the value until a reload of the file). A store lock guards the game thread's changes. A write of a store that is large with the sections' default rows puts only the store's keys in the file, as row `0010-ini-store-256` says. Test `runtime_settings_dirty`. |
| arceus-temporal-probe | `gpu/vk/temporal.c`, pure rules in `gpu/vk/temporal_math.h`. `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL=probe` (unset: none of the temporal code runs). For Pokémon Legends: Arceus in the Vulkan renderer. It learns the scene's colour and depth targets from the frame itself, reads the camera's matrices, makes camera motion vectors in a pass of its own and logs numbers about them (`arceus-temporal` lines). The picture is unchanged unless `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL_VIEW=1` or `2` is set (default 0). Test `temporal_math`. See `docs/dev/engine/motion-vector.md`. |
| arceus-temporal-taa | `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL=taa`: the scene's camera is jittered by one of eight sub-pixel offsets a frame, through a copy of the camera block in the frame's staging memory (the game's memory is not changed), and the scene is resolved with a history at the scene's size. Options, each off unless set: `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL_NEAREST=1`, `_HISTORY=catmull` (default linear), `_CLAMP=variance` (default minmax), `_BLEND=adaptive` (default fixed 0.1), `_LUMA=1`, `_SHARPEN=<0 to 1>` (default 0), `_MIPBIAS=<0 to -2>` (default unset: with `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL_RECT=1` the automatic bias, else none; a number from 0 to -2 is a set value), `_VIEW=3` or `4`. Shaders `shaders/temporal_*.frag`. None of the options is on by default. |
| arceus-temporal-object-vectors | `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL_VECTORS=object` (default camera), with `probe` or `taa`: moving and skinned objects get motion vectors of their own, from the constant blocks their G-buffer draws bind. `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL_REJECT=1` (default off) refuses history where an object's own motion exceeds a bound. `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL_LINKS=1` (default off) learns which two slots a block takes in turn when they are further apart than one block. |
| arceus-temporal-rect | `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL_RECT=1` (default off): with a scene drawn into a rectangle of its targets (scene scale below 1) a frame goes through a gate that accepts it only when the rectangle, the fraction and the viewport agree, and all temporal passes work inside the rectangle. Without the switch such frames are left as drawn. With it, a negative `_MIPBIAS` is applied only in frames the gate accepted. |
| arceus-temporal-gputime | `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL_GPUTIME=1` (default off, read only): two timestamps around the temporal passes, and every 600 presents a line with the GPU time between them. Off, it adds no command and no query. |
| arceus-scene-scale | `SNX_ARCEUS_SCENE_SCALE` (default off: unset, or 1.0 and above, changes nothing): a number from 0.5 to below 1.0, or `p/q`, written once over the game's own default pair of 3D buffer scales before the game's code runs (`runtime/arceus_scene_scale.h`, called from `arceus_clock.c`). It needs the fixed resolution (on unless `SNX_ARCEUS_FIXED_RESOLUTION` is set to a value other than `1`) and refuses with a line without it. `gpu/vk/scene_scale.c` is read only: it logs the fraction and the viewports the game then uses. See `docs/records/game/arceus-timing.md`, section "Scene scale". |
| vk-rec-direct | `gpu/vk/record.c`: new function `vk_rec_direct(cb, before, direct, user)`. It hands the frame's command buffer to code that records with Vulkan calls of its own: the recording thread's work is drained first, the callback runs, and the answer says whether it ran, refused, failed or had no buffer. Used only by the upscaler's hand-over. In the same file, an inherited fault is fixed on its own: the recorder copied a barrier's empty arrays with `memcpy(NULL, 0)`. Fixture `tests/vk_record/run.sh` (Linux, address and thread sanitizers, not part of the test run on Windows). |
| arceus-upscaler-contract | `gpu/vk/upscaler.h`: the contract between the runtime and an upscaler library's adapter, version 5 (`SNX_UPSCALER_ABI`), with the size and place of every member that crosses asserted for each compiler. `gpu/vk/upscaler_module.c`: loads an adapter that is a module of its own (DLSS's, built apart with Microsoft's compiler from the user's own SDK) by its full path beside the program, hands it the host's log and reads its table's version first. The self-test (`SNX_ARCEUS_UPSCALER_SELFTEST=dlss`) and the game (`SNX_ARCEUS_UPSCALER=dlss`) load it, once a session. `gpu/vk/upscaler_host.c`: which adapter a name means, and what the instance and the device have to be made with for it. `gpu/vk/upscaler_fsr.cpp` (Windows builds only): the adapter for FSR 3.1 through the FidelityFX API, built against the SDK's API headers in `third_party/FidelityFX-SDK`. The SDK's library (`amd_fidelityfx_loader_vk.dll`) is never in this repository: the user puts it beside the program, and without it the adapter says "not available". `gpu/vk/upscaler_xess.cpp` (Windows builds only): the adapter for XeSS Super Resolution, built against Intel's MIT headers in `third_party/XeSS`, whose library (`libxess.dll`) the user puts beside the program in the same way. Nothing of this runs without one of the two switches below. |
| arceus-upscaler-selftest | `SNX_ARCEUS_UPSCALER_SELFTEST=fsr`, `dlss` or `xess` (default off: `0`, `off` and unset leave the mode off): the program does not load the game. On a Vulkan instance and device of its own, without a window, it drives the adapter with generated scenes whose true picture is known and writes lines that begin with `arceus-upscaler-selftest`, ending with `RESULT: PASS` or `FAIL` and the process's exit code. Case 7 needs the validation layer with its synchronisation checks asked for and no message. `gpu/vk/upscaler_selftest.c`, pure parts in `upscaler_selftest.h`. Its result is FAIL for FSR and PASS for XeSS. For DLSS it runs an integration matrix that judges no quality, and its result is FAIL with one known library deviation (the reset at 1/2). Regression generators `tests/upscaler_selftest_callbacks` (Linux). |
| arceus-upscaler-dlss | `msvc/upscaler_dlss/` (new): DLSS's adapter as a module of its own, `snx_upscaler_dlss.dll`, built with Microsoft's compiler only when the builder gives the path of their own DLSS SDK (`SNX_DLSS_SDK_DIR`). Nothing of the SDK is in this repository, and the built module, which holds NVIDIA's static library, stays on the machine that built it. The build fails if the module imports `vulkan-1.dll`. It is the DLSS adapter of the contract above: NGX's start for the game's device, a feature per configuration, its evaluate and its shutdown, with the lifetimes and the frame's numbers in pure headers (`dlss_core.h`, `dlss_eval.h`, `dlss_record.h`) that `tests/upscaler_boundary` runs against a stand-in NGX. DLSS's runtime is NVIDIA's, which NGX finds at run time: it is not in this repository and not built here. |
| arceus-upscaler-game | `SNX_ARCEUS_UPSCALER=fsr`, `dlss` or `xess` (default off), needs `SNX_ARCEUS_TEMPORAL=taa` and is refused with `_REJECT=1`. Experimental. At full size in frames whose scene is the whole target, and below it with the fixed resolution (on unless `SNX_ARCEUS_FIXED_RESOLUTION` is set to a value other than `1`) and a scene scale of 1/2, 3/5, 2/3, 3/4 or 4/5 (`docs/dev/engine/ai-upscaling.md`): the frame's colour, depth and motion vectors are handed to the library through `vk_rec_direct`, the library writes a private `R32G32B32A32_SFLOAT` image, and a pass of ours (`shaders/temporal_upscaled.frag`) writes it into the scene colour. Our own resolve, sharpen, history and views do not run with it. A stop is for the rest of the session and leaves every frame as the game draws it. `SNX_ARCEUS_TARGET_FPS` gives the frame time when none was measured. In `gpu/vk/surface.c` the write masks of the image tracker gained `VK_ACCESS_2_MEMORY_WRITE_BIT`, the access named for work the runtime did not record itself. Lines begin with `arceus-upscaler`. |
| arceus-upscaler-device-needs | Only with `SNX_ARCEUS_UPSCALER` naming an adapter: `gpu/vk/device.c` asks the adapter what it needs of the device and the host checks the answer itself (`gpu/vk/upscaler_needs.h`, pure): extension names against the physical device's list, two accepted feature structures (compute shader derivatives, and the mutable descriptor type for XeSS), and the core feature bits `upscaler.h` defines (separate depth and stencil layouts first, the others for DLSS and XeSS). If anything refuses, or the device cannot be made with the additions, it is made as without the switch. The upscaler starts only when its needs are in the record of what the device was made with. Without the switch the device is made from the same list and chain as before. |
| vk-validation-lines | With the existing option `vk_validation` (setting `vulkan_validation_layer`, default 0) only. The game's instance also asks for the layer's synchronisation checks and asks the layer's limit of repeated messages off, each through an extension the layer itself lists. Lines that begin with `arceus-validation:` say what the run has: the layer, the checks, the callback, the limit, each callback that is the first of its rule or names a variable's name not seen before, counts at 1, 2, 4, 8 and so on, and each limit that was met (`gpu/vk/validation_lines.h`, pure, with the fixture `tests/validation_lines`). Each callback keeps its old `vulkan validation:` line. Inherited code changed for it: `common/gpu/vk/vk_common.c` `snx_vk_instance_create`, shared with the other frontends, has new fields in `SnxVkInstanceInfo` and `SnxVkInstance` and reads the layer list through `snx_vk_layer_search`, which asks an incomplete list again. That runs only when validation was asked for: without the option the same calls are made as before. |
| arceus-screenshot-lock | The screenshot holds `vk_lock` only for the readback of the last presented frame: the pixels are copied out of the reused readback memory, and the hash and the `.ppm` file are made after the lock is let go, so the GPU thread is not held for them (about 165 ms every screenshot before). `vkr_screenshot` and `shot.h`; test `arceus_shot` checks the hash and the file against the earlier code. |
| arceus-discord-bare | On by default (`SNX_ARCEUS_DISCORD_BARE` is on unless set to a value other than `1`): Discord presence also without the timing layer (the game's own 30 FPS, another refused target, or `SNX_ARCEUS_TIMING_FIXES=0`). Its tick runs on the clock read's dispatch entry (`main+278303c`) with no word of the game changed, and two counters stand in for the two fixes on their own JIT bodies (`main+193c04c` camera input, `main+9dbeac` battle sequence), each with the fix's guards. The readers and the host half are the same as with the layer. |
| arceus-pass-census | `SNX_PASS_CENSUS=1` (or `SNX_ARCEUS_PASS_CENSUS=1`): read-only, the Vulkan renderer logs two frames in a row every 1200 presents from the 900th, up to 10 times, the passes in order with their targets, viewports, programs, samples and marks, and the vertex constant blocks, streams, feedback and compute of geometry passes. `gpu/vk/render.c`; `docs/dev/engine/arceus-pass-census.md`. |
| arceus-perf-play-set | The eight `SNX_ARCEUS_PERF_*` switches of the FPS play set are on by default: `SNX_ARCEUS_PERF_LANDING=3`, `_PERF_REPLAY=3`, `_PERF_INPLACE=4`, `_PERF_COMPARE=2`, `_PERF_QUERY=1`, `_PERF_SAMPLE=1`, `_PERF_SCAN=1` and `_PERF_STORAGE=1` (`release.c`). Unset gives the switch's default level, one of its levels gives that level, and any other value gives 0 (`perf_level`). The replay's bind walks, the draw words, the query reports, the sampled hashes, the landing's changed runs, the list marks, the release walks and the in-place reads then run in their fast paths. See `docs/dev/engine/nvn-vulkan.md`. |
| arceus-perf-log-switches | Log and profile switches, off unless set: `SNX_ARCEUS_PERF_TIMES` (1 or 2), `SNX_ARCEUS_PERF_PROBES`, `SNX_ARCEUS_FRAME_LOG`, `SNX_ARCEUS_LATENCY_PROBE`, `SNX_ARCEUS_PROFILE` (the `profiler` option), `SNX_ARCEUS_GPU_PROFILE` (the `vk_gpu_profile` option), `SNX_ARCEUS_VK_VALIDATION` and `SNX_ARCEUS_PATCH_HASH`. `main.c`; see `docs/dev/engine/nvn-vulkan.md`. |
| md3-menu-core | Phase 7.5, unit 4. The MD3 core of the engine menu (`docs/dev/ui/engine-menu.md`) in `src/nx/gpu/vk/md3/`: the HCT palette, the UI scale, the theme, the motion and the widgets, built into `snx_vk` with the host tests `md3_palette`, `md3_motion` and `md3_scale`. Nothing calls it yet. |
| engine-menu-shell | Phase 7.5, unit 4b. The engine menu shell (`src/nx/gpu/vk/engine_menu.{h,cpp}`, `docs/dev/ui/engine-menu.md`). One atomic state (open, closing, closed) opens and closes it; `engine_menu_choice` picks the legacy menu with `imgui=0` or `legacy_menu=1`, the engine menu with `imgui=1`, `legacy_menu=0` and its windows running, and no menu when the windows did not start. F2, Back, Guide, the scripted Home press and the on-screen menu button open and close it while `imgui=1` and `legacy_menu=0`; without the windows they do nothing and one line names the reason. While it is open or closing the game gets no key, mouse, gamepad or finger input (`sdl3.c` gate, `g_menu_held*`, `keys_release_all`); the first finger drives the ImGui pointer as the mouse's left button, the mouse capture is released, and a still frame is refreshed. A key-up is never taken from the game, so a key that went down comes up. SDL gamepad buttons and axes map to `ImGuiKey_Gamepad*` in a pure rule and go through the `imgui_input` queue; the last input device names the bottom bar hints. The frame computes `md3::UiScale` from the window's pixel height and `overlay_display_percent`, applies the MD3 theme only while the panel draws and restores the saved style. The icon font `fonts/MaterialSymbolsRounded-Subset.ttf` merges like the Japanese font; a missing file is logged once. The shell is the full-screen panel of the mockup (title, rail of 10 pages, page fade and slide, panel motion, rail indicator, hints crossfade, smooth scroll, Close, B and Esc, Reduce motion on the Display page); each page shows one placeholder card. The panel draws into an offscreen image of the swapchain's format and size (premultiplied, since ImGui's blend over the transparent clear leaves premultiplied color), and a full-screen triangle (`shaders/menu_composite.*`) composites it with `ONE / ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA` and the panel alpha. The image is freed with `vk_defer_image` on an extent change and in `vk_imgui_swapchain_gone`. Tests: `engine_menu`, `imgui_input`. |
| crash-library-windows | A host crash in a library on Windows names the DLL, the offset from its base and the thread kind, and lists up to 24 host frames as DLL and offset, the same as the POSIX branch (`report_place` in `crash.c`, helper `module_of_address`). `GetModuleHandleExW` and `GetModuleFileNameW` can take the loader lock, so a crash while another thread holds it can stop the report; `dladdr` on POSIX has the same limit. A user run of the engine menu named `nvoglv64.dll` and the calling engine function this way. |
| engine-menu-display-pages | Phase 7.5, unit 5, first move. The Display and Performance pages of the engine menu show the rows of the settings model, and each row takes the widget that the model picks (`docs/dev/ui/engine-menu.md`, section 4). The Performance page shows five main rows, then the other rows under "Advanced". A number field edits an int row, and its edit rules are in the same section. The text of a list row wraps before its right part, and every list row reserves the restart icon slot. Files: `src/nx/gpu/vk/menu_settings.{h,cpp}` (the widget rule, the Performance groups and the number parse), `src/nx/gpu/vk/md3/md3_layout.{h,cpp}` (the text column, the row height and the page scroll target), `src/nx/gpu/vk/md3/md3_widgets.{h,cpp}` (`NumberField` and the list row), `src/nx/gpu/vk/engine_menu.cpp` (the two pages and the nav and rail scroll), `src/nx/gpu/vk/imgui_settings.{c,h}` (the window of each page, `IMGUI_WINDOW_ENGINE_MENU`). Tests: `menu_settings` and `md3_layout` (new), and `imgui_settings` (updated for the window of each page). The old Display window keeps only Graphics. The user ran the engine menu at 2000x1088 and at 1280x720 and confirmed the pages, the layout and the number field. |
| engine-menu-graphics-page | Phase 7.5, unit 5, second move. The Graphics page shows the rows of the settings model in model order. The old Display window, its menu item and the window value `IMGUI_WINDOW_DISPLAY` are deleted. Files: `src/nx/gpu/vk/engine_menu.cpp` (the Graphics page, `DrawSettingsPage` shared with the Display page), `src/nx/gpu/vk/imgui_settings.{c,h}` (the window of the Graphics page), `src/nx/gpu/vk/imgui_ui.cpp` (the removal of the window). Tests: `imgui_settings` (updated: the window of each page, and the pages of each window in model order). The user ran the engine menu and confirmed the seven rows, the D-pad navigation, the apply and the save of the values, and the restart mark of the three startup rows. |
| arceus-text-wait | On by default with the text tick (`SNX_ARCEUS_TEXT_TICK_END=0` turns it off, `1` and `3` keep it on, and any other value logs one line and keeps it on). On a frame that is not a text's tick, the glyph step (`main+2B315E8` from `main+FBFC24`) of a text whose last real step answered other than 1 (a wait: the end of the text, a page break, closed) runs the game's step, so the press tests `main+FC10E4` and `main+FC1078` see a press on any frame. A text being revealed is skipped as before. In the end wait of modes 2 and 3 the auto-advance count `+A3` (`main+2B31D44`) stays on the tick: an extra step that would complete it is skipped, and one that counted gets the byte back. `arceus-text-tick: end=3` every 5 s with the steps run, the counts held and the steps kept back, and with `SNX_ARCEUS_TEXT_PROBE=1` a line when a text enters and leaves an auto-advance wait. Tests `arceus_clock`. See `docs/records/game/arceus-timing.md`. |
